clue.text: Tibetan monks said they might give you wool

indicators.note: what is said is spoken out loud, so we want a word that sounds like this one rather than one spelt like it

blocks.note: lamas are Buddhist monks of Tibet; the South American animals sound identical

explanation.surface: A curious claim that monks in Tibet are a source of wool.
explanation.walkthrough: The monks are LAMAS with one L; the woolly animals are LLAMAS with two, pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids kept partly for their fleece, which is spun into yarn.

clue.text: Writer of essays about jump cut

blocks.note: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia
c. for circa, Latin for about
to hop is to jump

explanation.surface: An essayist writing about a jump cut in film editing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' sits at the end looking like part of 'jump cut', a film editing term, but it is the definition: a cut of meat. Charles Lamb is the essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a portion of meat sliced from the rib or loin, which butchers call a cut.

clue.text: The French tucked into wine after creepy-crawly with bony outgrowths

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it, so one piece sits within the other
coming after means placed later in the word, so the order of the chunks is fixed

blocks.note: an ant is a small insect, a creepy-crawly
le is French for 'the'
red is a wine

explanation.surface: A French person sipping wine after spotting an insect, oddly with bony growths.
explanation.walkthrough: The French article slots into the gap where the insect meets the wine, rather than inside the wine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Antlers are the branched bony growths on a deer's head, so an antlered stag carries them.

clue.text: Menu with quail: aunt ordered, given steer, some time in September

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence
being given something means having it added, so one more piece is attached at the end

blocks.note: the words menu, quail and aunt, taken letter for letter
a steer is a castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: An aunt orders quail from a menu and is served beef, at some point in September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and the colon simply string the three fodder words together; 'given' then attaches the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The autumnal equinox, when day and night are equal length, falls around 22 or 23 September in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Port, and a few lines of poetry

blocks.note: first meaning: a port city on the River Shannon in Ireland
second meaning: a comic five-line verse form

explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' tempts toward the fortified wine; here it is a harbour town, the Irish city on the Shannon estuary.
explanation.definitionFit: The city lends its name to the humorous five-line rhyming verse, and it is a harbour on the Shannon.

clue.text: Country where Everyman was a contender

blocks.note: the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I
someone who ran in a race or election was a contender

explanation.surface: A country where the setter once competed for a title.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often mean themselves by their pseudonym, so Everyman is I; 'I ran' says the setter was a contender.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly known as Persia, so it is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Type of Christian festival given direction: do up old cross

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
being given something means having it added, so the next piece follows on

blocks.note: Easter is the main Christian festival
north is a compass direction
taken as written
O is an abbreviation for old
an X is a cross

explanation.surface: Instructions for a church festival: refurbish an old cross.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do up' looks like 'renovate', but the word is read upwards in this down entry. The word break falls unexpectedly inside the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern Orthodox Christians belong to the family of churches of Greece, Russia and eastern Europe, a major branch of the faith.

clue.text: Impetuous Cretan? Absolutely! Regretful under sun, primarily!

definitions.text: Impetuous Cretan? Absolutely! Regretful under sun, primarily!

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so we keep only the opening letter of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Impetuous Cretan? Absolutely! Regretful under sun
blocks.note: the opening letters of these six words

explanation.surface: A rash young man from Crete, full of regret beneath the sun.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the first letters spell the name, and the words tell his story of flying too close to the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Icarus escaped Crete on wax wings, ignored his father's warning and fell when the sun melted them.

clue.text: Pretend to have mounting appetite for offal

indicators.note: in a down entry, mounting means climbing upward, so the letters read bottom to top
to have something is to hold it alongside, so the next piece is joined on

blocks.note: to kid is to pretend or tease
a yen is a craving or appetite

explanation.surface: Someone faking a growing hunger for organ meat.
explanation.walkthrough: KID followed by YEN read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the edible internal organs of an animal, and kidney is one such organ eaten as food.

clue.text: Change Greek character with brief thank-you note

blocks.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
ta is short, informal British for thank you
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Updating a Greek letter by adding a quick thank-you note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thank-you note' reads as one thing, a letter of thanks, but it splits into the informal thanks and the sol-fa note.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form or nature, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Roughly sand that item of furniture

indicators.note: rough handling knocks things out of shape, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to give a piece of furniture a rough sanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly sand' sounds like woodwork advice; 'roughly' is the signal and 'sand that' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatstand is a tall freestanding pole with hooks for coats and hats, a piece of household furniture.

clue.text: Composer's intro mostly sassy, regularly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
at regular intervals means every other letter, so alternate ones are kept

blocks.note: a debut is a first appearance, an introduction
first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A composer's opening bars described as rather cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay: DEBU(T) with SSY from the odd letters of sassy.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Debussy was the French composer of Clair de lune and La mer, an impressionist of music.

clue.text: Élite ate up scones etc.

indicators.note: when things are up they are amiss or in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the cream is the best, the elite
taken as written

explanation.surface: The upper class polished off scones and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ate up' reads as 'devoured'; instead the three letters are disordered. A cream tea is a British afternoon tea of scones with clotted cream and jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A cream tea is the meal itself, and scones with jam and cream are its main parts, so 'scones etc.' describes it.

clue.text: Pass up garbage

blocks.note: first meaning: to decline an offer
second meaning: rubbish

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently, a verb stressed on the second syllable and a noun stressed on the first.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass up a chance is to decline it, and household rubbish is called refuse in formal British usage.

clue.text: Who's beginning to shun wordiest mess?

definitions.text: Who's beginning to shun wordiest mess?

indicators.note: to shun the beginning is to avoid the opening letter, so the first one is dropped
a mess is a jumble, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written before its first letter goes

explanation.surface: A question about who first steers clear of the most verbose muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: drop the W of 'wordiest' and rearrange, and the question itself describes people who cut wordy messes.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors are the people whose job is to tidy and trim rambling copy, so they avoid verbose clutter.

clue.text: More than one pastry poet's finishing off – plenty, and then some!

indicators.note: to finish something off here is to lose its finish, so the last letter is cut

blocks.note: over means more than
a means one
a bun is a small sweet bake
Dante Alighieri, the Italian poet

explanation.surface: Several pastries plus a poet polishing off his plate: more than enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one pastry' looks like a plural, but it is read literally as OVER A BUN. Dante loses his E.
explanation.definitionFit: Overabundant means present in excessive quantity, which is having plenty with extra to spare.

clue.text: Most angry if secret gets out

indicators.note: something that gets out is loose and unruly, so these letters break free of their order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone becomes furious when their confidence is leaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets out' reads as a secret leaking, which fits the surface perfectly; it is the signal to rearrange 'if secret'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce can describe violent temper, so the superlative fits a person in the greatest rage.

clue.text: To go all the way over pub – that's some bike!

definitions.note: a part of a bike, not the whole bicycle

blocks.clueFragment: To go all the way over
blocks.note: to cross is to go from one side to the other
a bar is a pub

explanation.surface: A cyclist so impressed by a ride that will carry them across to the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's some bike!' sounds like admiration, but 'some' means a part of the bike.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossbar is the horizontal tube of a bicycle frame joining saddle post to handlebar post, one component.

clue.text: Hire wrestler for training, one with wiry hair

indicators.note: training puts something through drills to reshape it, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Hiring a wrestler as a sparring partner, a scruffy-haired one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One with wiry hair' sounds like the wrestler; it is the definition, a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Welsh terrier is a dog breed with a dense, wiry black-and-tan coat, so it is one with wiry hair.

clue.text: Former US press secretary to add excitement to start of race

indicators.note: the start of something is its opening, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: to spice up is to make more exciting
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A former White House spokesman livening up the opening of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: SPICE followed by R. Sean Spicer was White House press secretary in 2017.
explanation.definitionFit: Sean Spicer served as White House press secretary early in the first Trump administration.

clue.text: One after another in accident and emergency

indicators.note: in means contained inside, so the letters sit within the words that follow

blocks.note: running across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Patients arriving one after another at the casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: Accident and emergency is the British name for a hospital casualty ward, so the phrase reads naturally as a place.
explanation.definitionFit: In tandem means one behind the other, as on a tandem bicycle, so arranged in sequence.

clue.text: Exercise, having ingested rich sauce somewhere in Czech Republic

indicators.note: what is ingested is swallowed and held within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: PE is physical education
ragu is a rich Italian meat sauce

explanation.surface: A workout after a heavy meal somewhere in the Czech Republic.
explanation.walkthrough: PE stands for physical education, the school subject; ragu is an Italian meat sauce such as Bolognese.
explanation.definitionFit: Prague is the capital city of the Czech Republic, so it is one place located there.

clue.text: Where to find fruit or vegetables?

blocks.note: taken as written
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A shopper asking where the fruit and veg are kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit or vegetables' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops after 'fruit' and the little conjunction is kept literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchards are plantations of fruit trees, so they are places where apples and pears grow.

clue.text: Spanish kingdom's Christmas Rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means moving upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Noel is a name for Christmas

explanation.surface: A medieval Spanish realm celebrating a Christmas uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: León was a medieval kingdom of north-west Spain, later united with Castile.

clue.text: Around church, timeless descant arranged to offer musical endings

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it, so one piece wraps the other
time is abbreviated T, so being without time means that letter is removed
to arrange is to set in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written before T is removed
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: In church, a choir's descant is reworked to provide closing phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time, so 'timeless' strips it out before the remaining letters are rearranged around the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is the chord sequence closing a musical phrase, so cadences are musical endings.

clue.text: Commercial almost exceedingly bold: scandalously, perhaps?

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
very means exceedingly
B is the abbreviation for bold type

explanation.surface: A daring advert, one that might be called scandalous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scandalously' looks like a comment on the advert; it is an example of the answer, flagged by 'perhaps'. VERY loses Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandalously ends in -ly and modifies a verb, making it an instance of an adverb.

clue.text: Adjusting recordings of rock band Nine Inch Nails' guitarists' intros

indicators.note: an intro is the opening, so only the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: R.E.M. was an American rock band
IX is nine in Roman numerals
the opening letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: Remastering tracks by the band Nine Inch Nails with guitar openings.
explanation.walkthrough: Nine Inch Nails is a real band, so the name reads as one unit; it is broken apart, with Nine giving IX and the rest supplying initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To remix is to rebalance or rework the separate tracks of a recording into a new version.

clue.text: Henry's uncle, divorcee, chopped up tree

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into bits, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a divorcee is someone's ex
taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal relative, newly divorced, felling a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke of Exeter, Thomas Beaufort, was uncle to King Henry V and appears in Shakespeare's play; he is usually just called Exeter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Henry V the character Exeter is the king's uncle, so the title identifies him.
